hints: Look closely at the polar groups in the repeat unit, the nitrile and the ester, and ask what kind of dipoles they create.
Remember that temporary dipole forces are present in all solids, while permanent dipole forces need polar bonds like $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ and $\text{C=O}$.
Check for hydrogen bonding carefully by asking if there is any H attached directly to N, O or F to act as a donor.
walkthrough:
**Spot the forces that are always there**

All solids, even non-polar ones, have temporary dipole - induced dipole forces (London forces) from momentary uneven electron distribution. This polymer has many electrons, so statement 1 is definitely true.

**Look for permanent dipoles**

The repeat unit contains two strongly polar groups. The nitrile group $\text{-C}\equiv\text{N}$ and the ester group $\text{-CO}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ both contain very electronegative N and O atoms.

Polar bond examples:
$$\text{C}^{\delta+} - \text{N}^{\delta-} \quad \text{and} \quad \text{C}^{\delta+} = \text{O}^{\delta-}$$

**Test for hydrogen bonding**

Hydrogen bonding needs H bonded directly to N, O or F as a donor, plus a lone pair on N, O or F as an acceptor. Here all H atoms are on carbon ($\text{C-H}$), and there is no $\text{O-H}$ or $\text{N-H}$ group.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{H-bond donor required: H-N, H-O, or H-F}$$

**Put it together**

Statement 1 is true and statement 2 is true because of the polar nitrile and ester groups. Statement 3 is false because there is no suitable H-bond donor. So only 1 and 2 apply.

options.A: Incorrect. This suggests 1, 2 and 3 are all present. While 1 and 2 are correct, 3 is wrong because the polymer has no $\text{O-H}$ or $\text{N-H}$ bonds to donate a hydrogen bond, only $\text{C-H}$, $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ and ester groups.
options.B: Correct. Temporary dipole forces (1) exist in every solid polymer, and permanent dipole forces (2) exist due to the polar $\text{CN}$ and $\text{CO}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ groups. Hydrogen bonds (3) are absent as there is no H attached to N, O or F.
options.C: Incorrect. This suggests 2 and 3 only. It correctly includes permanent dipoles but wrongly includes hydrogen bonds and wrongly leaves out temporary dipole forces, which are always present.
options.D: Incorrect. This suggests only 1 is present. It misses the important permanent dipole to permanent dipole interactions from the highly polar nitrile and carbonyl parts of the ester group.
